approved_scopes: The incidence map on a tree is injective on edge flows, has image 1-perp, and the stated head-side cut sum has the correct sign.

On a tree, edge differences modulo 2pi uniquely determine a phase-torus class modulo common phase. Hence strict feasibility gives exactly 2^(n−1) locked classes; saturated edges reduce the count by one binary choice each.

B^T restricted to 1-perp is an isomorphism, so Sylvester congruence with diag(Kcos(delta)) gives the precise Hessian inertia and q unstable directions for q negative cosines. The sign reversal from Hessian to dynamics is correct.
The mean-frequency rotating frame and the local rather than global potential argument are appropriately scoped. The local convex-ball proof yields genuine nonlinear local exponential stability.
The edge-flow derivative, mean-zero phase sensitivity norm and cut Rayleigh upper bound are correct; the rational q-family and rate-times-sensitivity interval follow with the stated constants.

Full edge observation loses only common phase locally; uniform natural-frequency shifts are invisible to relative measurements. The center-only star pair motion exactly cancels at the sensor and supplies a nonlinear blindness example, not only a linearized one.

issues.description: The extension says projection matrices become rational when B and Sigma are rational. The noncentrality quadratic-form matrix B^T(BSigmaB^T)^(-1)B is rational, but the Euclidean orthogonal projection in whitened coordinates contains Sigma^(1/2) and need not be rational. Example Sigma=diag(1,2), B=(1,1) gives P=(1/3)[[1,sqrt2],[sqrt2,2]]. The inverse formula also needs full row rank of B or a pseudoinverse convention.
issues.fix: Specify full-row-rank B; say the noncentrality quadratic-form matrix is rational for rational B,Sigma. Distinguish it from the whitened orthogonal projector, whose entries can be algebraic. State a pseudoinverse if redundant measurement rows are allowed.
